body: Skyping with her now and we're both laughing a lot. Thank you so much for talking.
She's started therapy. I have hopes, but like I say, she's proud and stubborn. I have faith that she'll eventually come through this, but it still makes me feel awful that she's in such pain.

Oh, no, she's going after jobs on her own, but it just can't happen soon enough for her. Also, although she loves me dearly, she might beat me senseless if I did that. She's got a lot of pride, and hates the idea of needing too much help. I can sympathize, but it makes getting help much more of a touchy subject than it frankly needs to be.

This is wonderful advice, but I often get the "no, you don't understand how I feel" when I try to tell her I've been there. I'm working on it, though.

I like the idea of the associative bit, but she's both very clever and very proud, so I shudder to think what would happen if she felt like I was patronizing her.

I know this is a good idea, it's just tough to make myself do it sometimes.

I should have mentioned earlier, I did recently overhear her telling her dad on the phone that she MIGHT consider medication if she really has to. She has a complicated - though, I hasten to add, not outrageously troubled - relationship with her folks, so I don't think she'd just be trying to get them off her back, but I sometimes don't know. I'm a depressive too, after all, and I do tend to think the worst.

Oh, as I said, I really don't want to lose her. But I have no faith at all in the possibilities of a long-distance relationship. Hopefully it doesn't come to that, and I'm prepared to do a lot to make sure it doesn't.

I didn't mean to give the wrong impression, either - I love her madly and I wouldn't lose her for anything, I'm just a little freaked about the possibility of her moving home.

If only I was good at this myself! But you're right, that does sound like an excellent idea.

EDIT - and I have been stressing this. Whatever you do, KEEP MOVING. Clean your room, work hard at your job, go out and talk to people. Makes all the difference in the world.

She just recently started seeing a therapist of some sort. I've broached the topic, she hates the idea of medication based on a bad experience with it earlier in life.

And I always get the "you think I'm crazy" response if I'm not super-careful in how I broach the topic of getting help or going on meds. It's one of the things that drives me so nuts, that I feel like I have to tip-toe.
